nodes.title: Fix Red Light of Death: A Simple Guide to Restoring Your Board's Battery
nodes.body:
Stuck With a Board That Won't Turn On? Here's What's Really Happening Inside That Battery

That dreaded red light staring back at you is more than just annoying, it usually means your board is sitting in a corner instead of on the road. Before you assume the worst, it helps to understand what's actually going on inside the pack.

1. The Red Light of Death, Explained

If you ride an electric skateboard long enough, you'll eventually meet the Red Light of Death, commonly shortened to RLOD. It's the moment your board refuses to power on, and instead of the reassuring hum of your motor controller, you get a blinking or solid red indicator that seems to mean everything and nothing at once.

What's usually happening behind the scenes is a battery cell imbalance. Lithium battery packs are built from multiple individual cells wired together, and over time, through regular charging, discharging, and normal use, those cells can drift out of sync with each other. When the difference between cells gets too large, the battery management system inside your pack essentially throws up a wall to protect itself, and that wall shows up as a red light on your board.

The frustrating part is that this doesn't necessarily mean your battery is dead. In a lot of cases, the cells just need to be brought back into balance with one another. Without the right tool, though, riders can be stuck guessing, searching forums, or shipping their board off and waiting.

💡 Key insight: A red light doesn't always mean a dead battery, it often means unbalanced cells that simply need to be realigned.

2. Why Cell-Balancing Tools Matter for Electric Skateboard Owners

This is where a dedicated battery restore tool comes into the picture. Instead of treating RLOD as a mystery or a reason to buy a whole new battery pack, a purpose-built module lets you check what's actually happening at the cell level and correct it directly.

For anyone who rides regularly, this kind of tool changes the relationship you have with your board. Rather than being at the mercy of a single warning light, you get a way to diagnose the issue yourself, at home, without needing to be an electrical engineer. It turns a confusing failure into a straightforward, guided process.

It also shifts the mindset around battery issues in general. Instead of assuming the worst the moment something goes wrong, you have a first step to try, one that's designed specifically for the kind of battery packs used in electric skateboards.

3. How the Bert Touch XR Battery Restore Module Fits In

The BoostedUSA Bert Touch XR Battery Restore module was built specifically to deal with this exact scenario. It's designed for XR-style batteries and works by checking and balancing your battery cells, aiming to clear RLOD and get your board functional again.

Using it is meant to be simple. You disconnect your battery from the motor controller, plug it into the Bert Touch, and follow the on-screen instructions from there. Once connected, the module works to balance the cells automatically, so you're not manually adjusting anything yourself, you just let it do its job.

  • Plug-and-go design means you follow on-screen prompts instead of guessing at wiring or settings.
  • Automatic cell balancing takes the manual troubleshooting out of your hands once it's connected.
  • Built specifically for XR batteries, giving owners of that battery type a tool made with their setup in mind.

If you've been staring at a red light wondering whether your riding days are over, it might be worth learning more about how this module works with your specific battery setup. Keep in mind it's currently built for XR batteries and is not yet compatible with SR or Rev packs, so it's worth confirming your battery type before moving forward.

nodes.title: How to Restore Power to Your Electric Skateboard Motor
nodes.body:
Your Electric Skateboard Feels Dead — Here's Why You Shouldn't Give Up On It

There's nothing more frustrating than a board that used to fly down the street now sitting in the corner collecting dust. Before you write it off entirely, the fix might be simpler — and more affordable — than you think.

1. The Hidden Reason Your Ride Lost Its Edge

Electric skateboards are mechanical machines, and like any machine with moving parts, they wear down over time. The motor is one of the hardest-working components on the entire board — it spins thousands of times per ride, absorbs vibration from the road, and pushes through heat cycles every single session. Eventually, even a well-built motor will show signs of fatigue.

For Boosted board owners specifically, this is a familiar story. The brand built some of the most beloved electric skateboards ever made — the Stealth, the Plus, the Mini X, the Mini S — and riders put serious miles on them. A degraded motor can show up as reduced acceleration, a noticeable drop in top speed, strange noises under load, or a board that simply won't respond the way it used to. The riding experience goes from exhilarating to underwhelming fast.

The good news? In most cases, the rest of your board is perfectly fine. The deck, the trucks, the battery, the ESC — all of it can still be in great shape. Replacing a worn-out motor is often all it takes to bring the whole setup back to life, and that's a far more sensible path than hunting for a brand-new board in a discontinued lineup.

💡 Key Insight: A sluggish or unresponsive electric skateboard doesn't always mean the board is done — a single worn component like the motor is often the culprit, and swapping it out can restore the ride you remember.

2. Why the Right Replacement Motor Makes All the Difference

When it comes to replacing a motor on a precision-built electric skateboard, fit and compatibility aren't optional — they're everything. Boosted boards were engineered with specific tolerances, power curves, and mounting configurations. A motor that isn't purpose-built for your model won't just underperform; it can create new problems that compound the original issue.

That's exactly why an original replacement motor — one designed specifically for the Boosted platform — is the smartest choice for anyone looking to restore their board. You're not improvising or adapting something that was never meant to be there. You're putting back what was always supposed to be there, with the same power and reliability the board was designed around. The result is a ride that feels familiar in the best possible way: responsive, smooth, and confident under your feet.

There's also a practical side to this. Sourcing a compatible motor from a trusted channel means you're not gambling on fitment or guessing at specs. For riders who depend on their board for commuting, cruising, or just weekend fun, that peace of mind matters. Getting back on the road quickly — without a second round of troubleshooting — is worth a great deal.

3. What You Actually Get With a Quality Motor Replacement

  • Restored power and acceleration: A fresh motor brings back the punchy, responsive performance that made your Boosted board worth riding in the first place.
  • Broad model compatibility: This replacement motor is designed to work with the Boosted Stealth, Boosted Plus, Boosted Mini X, and Boosted Mini S — covering the most popular models in the lineup.
  • Cost-effective board revival: At $40 for one motor, you're investing a fraction of what a replacement board would cost to get your existing setup running like it should.
  • Confidence in every session: Riding on a motor you know is in good condition means you're not second-guessing every hill or long stretch — you can just focus on the ride.
  • Extends the life of your whole board: Replacing the motor gives every other well-maintained component on your board a reason to keep going, maximizing the value of everything you've already invested in it.

nodes.body:
Your Electric Skateboard Died — And It Might Not Be as Dead as You Think

One day your Boosted Board is running perfectly, and the next you're staring at a blinking red light that refuses to go away. Before you write off your ride entirely, there's something worth knowing.

1. The Red Light of Death: What It Is and Why It Happens

If you own a Boosted XR battery, there's a good chance you've heard the term "RLOD" thrown around in forums and Facebook groups. RLOD — short for Red Light of Death — is the nickname riders have given to a specific failure state where the battery refuses to charge, refuses to power the board, and just sits there flashing red like a tiny, infuriating stop sign.

The root cause is usually a cell imbalance inside the battery pack. Lithium-based battery packs are made up of multiple individual cells, and over time those cells can drift apart in their charge levels. When the gap between the highest and lowest cell gets wide enough, the battery management system throws up its hands and shuts everything down as a protective measure. The board isn't broken. The motor is fine. The ESC is fine. The battery just needs its cells brought back into alignment.

The frustrating part is that this can happen to a battery that still has plenty of usable life left in it. Riders who don't know about cell balancing often assume the pack is dead and start pricing out replacements — which, for a Boosted XR battery, is not a small expense. The good news is that in many cases, the battery is recoverable.

💡 Key Insight: A blinking red light on your Boosted XR battery is often a cell balance issue, not a sign that the pack is permanently dead — and that distinction can save you a significant amount of money.

2. Battery Restoration Tools: A Category Worth Understanding

Battery restoration modules are specialized devices designed to communicate with, diagnose, and in many cases actively correct the issues that cause battery packs to enter a fault state. For Boosted Board owners specifically, this category of tool has become increasingly relevant as the boards age and original manufacturer support has become harder to come by. When a brand stops producing hardware, the aftermarket community steps in — and that's exactly what's happened here.

What makes a dedicated restoration module different from simply trying to charge a dead pack with a standard charger is the level of interaction it has with the battery's internal systems. A restoration module can read individual cell voltages, identify which cells are out of balance, and apply a balancing process that brings everything back into a safe operating range.

The BoostedUSA Bert Touch XR is one of the tools that has emerged to serve this specific need. It's built around the idea that most XR battery failures caused by RLOD are fixable — and that the process of fixing them shouldn't require advanced technical knowledge or specialized lab equipment. The goal is to put a recovery process into the hands of everyday riders.

3. What the Bert Touch XR Actually Does for You

  • The connection process is straightforward — disconnect your battery from the motor controller, plug it into the Bert Touch, and follow the prompts — no soldering, no disassembly beyond what's already standard for battery removal.
  • It extends the usable life of a battery you've already invested in, which makes it a practical alternative to sourcing a replacement pack for an out-of-production board.
